title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a task force to oversee AI security and safeguards. It aims to coordinate efforts to protect critical infrastructure from AI‑related threats and promote secure AI practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to regulate the development, deployment, and use of AI technologies to reduce potential harms. It establishes safety standards, accountability measures, and cybersecurity safeguards so that AI systems are designed and operated responsibly, protecting public welfare and national security.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to protect electoral integrity by addressing potential AI‑driven deception. It proposes regulations, safeguards, and oversight mechanisms to detect and mitigate AI‑generated misinformation that could influence election processes.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is a proposed law that would establish a framework for governing the design, deployment, and operation of AI-controlled physical systems such as autonomous vehicles, drones, and industrial robots. It aims to ensure safety, interoperability, and accountability by setting standards, requiring coordination among manufacturers, operators, and regulators, and providing oversight for potential risks to public safety and privacy.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This proposal amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to increase transparency in political advertising. It would require ads that use AI-generated images or video to clearly disclose that generative AI was used.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating the use of artificial intelligence that could spread misinformation. It establishes rules and oversight to prevent AI-generated content from influencing voters or manipulating electoral processes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes rules for tracking and evaluating artificial intelligence systems that can autonomously improve themselves. It requires developers to provide transparency, conduct safety tests, and set up continuous monitoring to ensure these AI systems remain safe and aligned with human values.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to prevent the creation and use of artificial intelligence systems that could act unpredictably or cause harm. It seeks to set strict guidelines and oversight to ensure AI technologies remain safe, transparent, and aligned with human values.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to pause the construction and operation of new AI data centers until thorough environmental and societal impacts are assessed. It aims to protect ecosystems and ensure responsible use of resources while the policy framework for AI infrastructure is developed.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a new board to oversee and investigate cybersecurity and AI issues. The board will look into incidents, suggest policy changes, and promote safer, responsible use of AI.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a proposal to guide the development and deployment of artificial intelligence so that it benefits everyday Americans, emphasizing safety, fairness, and economic growth. It would set up rules and incentives that encourage ethical AI practices, protect privacy, and help create new jobs and opportunities for U.S. citizens.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a proposed law that would require Chinese companies and research institutions to produce regular, detailed reports on their AI systems’ capabilities, performance, and potential risks. Its goal is to promote transparency, protect national security, and give regulators the information they need to monitor and guide the rapid growth of artificial intelligence across industry and society.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 requires that medical professionals, not artificial intelligence systems, be the primary decision-makers for diagnosing and treating patients, ensuring that doctors retain ultimate responsibility for patient care. The law also sets limits on how AI can be used in healthcare, making sure it is only an assistant to a human clinician rather than a substitute for a doctor.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President. The office will oversee and coordinate efforts to identify, assess, and mitigate risks from AI and emerging technologies.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 seeks to make AI systems more dependable by setting clear safety and reliability standards for research and deployment. It establishes oversight mechanisms and encourages transparency to protect users from potential risks.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee and guide the U.S. government’s approach to AI. The committee will study AI’s societal impacts, advise Congress, and recommend policies and regulations to promote safe and responsible AI development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 sets out rules for identifying and measuring the risks that AI systems can pose. It requires companies to carry out formal risk assessments and share those results with regulators so that AI can be used safely and responsibly.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed piece of legislation that aims to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework for artificial intelligence. It seeks to balance innovation with safety by setting standards for AI development, deployment, and oversight, while protecting consumer rights and encouraging responsible use of the technology.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law aimed at addressing the environmental effects of artificial intelligence technologies. It establishes guidelines and regulatory measures to ensure AI systems operate sustainably and reduce their carbon footprint.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for teaching artificial‑intelligence concepts in elementary and secondary schools, mandating curriculum development, teacher training, and equitable access to technology resources. It also promotes research and collaboration between educational institutions, industry, and government to prepare students for an AI‑driven workforce.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a proposed federal law that establishes standards, oversight, and risk‑assessment protocols for AI research to ensure safety, reliability, and alignment with societal values. It calls for transparency in research practices, collaboration among industry, academia, and regulators, and the creation of a federal body to monitor compliance.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, via the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that employs AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also includes additional related provisions to support the overall goal of enhancing national cyber security.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students from kindergarten through twelfth grade with foundational knowledge and skills about artificial intelligence. It establishes standards for AI education, provides professional development for teachers, and allocates funding to ensure schools can deliver relevant, up‑to‑date curriculum that prepares students for a technology‑driven world.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is intended to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in handling veterans' claims, ensuring that AI tools are reliable, transparent, and fair. It sets out rules for oversight, data protection, and mechanisms for veterans to challenge decisions made by AI systems.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to clearly disclose how it uses artificial intelligence in veteran services. It mandates the agency to publish detailed explanations of the AI tools it employs, explain who is responsible for them, and provide veterans with a way to understand and challenge AI‑driven decisions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act proposes a nationwide effort to inform citizens about AI technology, its benefits, and its risks. It would create educational programs, resources, and outreach initiatives to improve public understanding and promote responsible use of AI.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The resolution emphasizes that the Senate believes religious freedom and the guidance of authoritative texts are vital in shaping how artificial intelligence systems are developed. It also calls for greater transparency in AI systems so that their operations and decisions can be openly understood and trusted.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a law designed to safeguard people from misleading or harmful AI systems. It requires companies to clearly disclose when they are using AI, explain how it works, and ensure that AI outputs are accurate and not designed to deceive users.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress on how artificial intelligence systems are used under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will cover AI’s role in acquiring, analyzing, querying, disseminating, or otherwise accessing information, providing oversight and transparency for these intelligence activities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 aims to enhance AI education across all levels of schooling and to prepare the workforce for an AI-driven economy. It proposes funding for teacher training, curriculum development, and partnerships between industry and educational institutions.
